metadata.title: User Guide for the TIMSS International Database: Final Year of Secondary School (Population 3) Data Collected in 1995-96

survey_design.weight_variable_name: TOTWGTL4 / TOTWGTM4 / TOTWGTP4 (and SENWGTx / HOUWGTx variants)
survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The document describes the TIMSS 1995-96 Population 3 international database for final-year secondary students, including sampling weights and guidance for secondary analysts. Students were selected via a two-stage design (schools sampled with PPS, then a fixed number of students sampled within schools), and sampling weights are provided to account for selection probabilities, stratification/disproportional sampling, and non-response adjustments. For achievement scale-score analyses, analysts are instructed to use the appropriate total student weights (TOTWGTL4 for literacy scale scores, TOTWGTM4 for advanced mathematics scale scores, TOTWGTP4 for physics scale scores), together with participation-status indicators (e.g., INTMSL4/INTMSM4/INTMSP4) to restrict to the relevant booklet-based subpopulation. For variance estimation, the guide specifies jackknife repeated replication (JRR) replicate weights and macros, and it also provides “senate” and “house” weight transformations (SENWGTx and HOUWGTx) to support different cross-country comparison conventions and to avoid deflated standard errors when software uses sample size rather than sum of weights.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This user guide documents TIMSS plausible values (five draws per scale) and the associated scaling/imputation framework, but it does not specify a separate missing-data imputation strategy for questionnaire or item nonresponse beyond the plausible-values methodology and the treatment of “not reached” responses during scaling. Because the document is a database user guide rather than an empirical ML study, it does not report a concrete missing-data handling method (e.g., listwise deletion or multiple imputation for missing covariates) for secondary analysts’ downstream models. Therefore, missing-data handling is not reported at the level required by the schema.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The guide defines TIMSS Population 3 (final year of secondary education) and explains that the international database includes achievement data (mathematics and science literacy, advanced mathematics, physics) and background data for participating countries in 1995-96. For scale-score analyses, analysts should restrict to the relevant booklet-based subpopulation using participation-status variables (INTMSL4/INTMSM4/INTMSP4 for scale scores; INTMSL/INTMSM/INTMSP for item-level scores) and apply the corresponding scale weights (TOTWGTL4/TOTWGTM4/TOTWGTP4). The test design assigns students to one 90-minute booklet based on whether they had taken advanced mathematics and/or physics (OO, OP, MO, MP), and the guide notes that “not reached” responses are treated as not administered during item calibration but as incorrect when computing student logit scores.

data.outcome_summary: This document is a TIMSS International Database User Guide (Population 3) describing how the TIMSS 1995-96 final-year secondary assessment is implemented and how to use the released international microdata for secondary analysis. It specifies the assessment structure (mathematics and science literacy for all final-year students; advanced mathematics for students who took advanced mathematics; physics for students who took physics), the booklet rotation design (four student preparation groups OO/OP/MO/MP), and the item pools and scoring approach (including two-digit coding for free-response items). Achievement scales are produced using IRT scaling with plausible values: five plausible values are drawn per scale and mapped to an international scale (mean 500, SD 100) for reporting. The guide also details the complex sampling design (two-stage school PPS then student sampling), provides multiple sampling weight variants (total, senate, house) for different cross-country comparison conventions, and recommends jackknife repeated replication (JRR) for standard error estimation. No predictive ML results are reported because the document is methodological documentation rather than an empirical study.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a database user guide/technical documentation rather than an empirical research paper. It does not estimate predictive models or report ML performance metrics, and it does not provide an analytic sample for a specific downstream outcome beyond describing how to select subpopulations and compute achievement scores. As a result, fields like total_students, ML techniques, confounders, and main findings are not applicable in the schema’s empirical-ML sense.
